newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
CBI CHIEF OFFERS TO QUIT

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Director Joginder Singh has offered to resign. This follows sharp differences in the government over the manner in which the CBI has been investigating an alleged Indian bank scam involving suspected unsecured loans. Sources said a decision on Joginder Singh's offer would be taken after Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda returned from Rome.
The Times Of India
KESRI-SONIA COMBINE MAY TILT BALANCE AGAINST RAO

Congress party sources are concerned over the growing rift between Sonia Gandhi, widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, and Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader Narasimha Rao. Party President Kesri was accused of waging a proxy war on behalf of Sonia Gandhi by Rao loyalists. Sources said supporters of the Sonia-Kesri combine were keen to capture CPP posts to diminish Rao's influence among party members. Instead of asking Rao to step down from the post, the combine would then pressurise Rao to quit. Antagonism between Kesri and Rao was highlighted when the CPP spokesman, a Rao appointee, held a separate press conference to declare Congress support for the Uttar Pradesh Presidential rule Bill.
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS PARTY REVOKES SUSPENSION

Congress President Sitaram Kesri revoked the suspensions of former ministers M.L. Fotedar and Sheila Dixit and former All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary K.N. Singh. The three, presently with the Congress-Tiwari, were suspended after the AICC session in April 1993 for demanding the implementation of the one-man one-post norm. Party sources said the party chief's move was yet another step towards bringing former Congressmen back into the party fold.
The Economic Times
CENTRAL BANK CLEARS 10 BILLION RUPEE FLOAT

Initial public offerings of Bank of India (BoI) and Corporation Bank totalling around 10 billion rupees were cleared by the central bank and the finance ministry. Both banks have received clearance to issue shares at a premium of 40 and 60 rupees each, respectively. BoI and Corporation Bank have been allowed to return 930 million rupees and 300 million rupees of the government capital, respectively. While BoI's 7.5 billion rupee issue is expected to hit the market at the end of December, Corporation Bank may enter with its 2.60 billion rupee issue in January 1997. Both banks will watch market response to Bank of Baroda's issue opening in the first week of December.
MINISTRY YET TO OK LINKAGES TO NAPHTHA-BASED POWER UNITS

The power ministry has yet to finalise the list of naphtha-based power projects which are to be awarded fuel linkages. The ministry had decided to finalise it by November 15 ahead of a March 31 deadline for submitting detailed reports. The power ministry had sent letters of request to state governments to evaluate the progress of the projects and recommend fuel linkages for them. The state governments have sent their feedback to the power ministry. The ministry is likely to give priority to projects which already have the techno-economic clearance and those which are expansions of the existing units.
PANEL SET UP TO DRAW BLUEPRINT FOR EXIM POLICY

The government has constituted a high-powered committee to suggest broad guidelines to be adopted in the new integrated Export Import (Exim) Policy 1997/2002. The existing Exim policy will have to be replaced by a new five-year policy on April 1, 1997. The committee is expected to look at ways to deal with the opening up of the trade sector, with India becoming an active member of the World Trade Organisation. The terms and reference of the committee include providing an operational definition of integrated Exim policy and laying down parameters for such a policy.
Financial Express
PROBE INTO IPRS VIOLATIONS BY INDIA

A World Trade Organisation (WTO) committee is coming to India to investigate charges of violation of Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs). The charges against India are not ratifying certain provisions of IPRs related to WTO, by the deadline, which expired in December, 1995. The investigation is being done following a complaint by two member nations of WTO.
INFLATION RATE FALLS MARGINALLY

Reversing the rising trend of the previous week, the inflation rate fell marginally to 6.48 percent during the week ended November 2. It was 6.57 percent the preceding week. The inflation rate has been in single digits for 84 weeks in succession since April 1, 1995. For the second successive week, the official wholesale price index for all commodities (base 1981/82) rose to 318.6, during the week ended November 2. It was 317.9 in the previous week.
Business Standard
BANK CREDIT JUMPS 17 BILLION RUPEES

In the fortnight ended October 25, 1996, bank credit turned positive for the first time, growing by 17.71 billion rupees to 2552.56 billion rupees, a rise of 0.7 percent. The rise over the March 31, 1996, level was just 0.5 percent at 12.41 billion rupee. In the corresponding period of last year, bank credit moved up by 6.8 percent at 143.8 billion rupee. The climb in bank credit is seen as a positive turn in the economy. The jump is basically attributed to the commencement of the busy season and lending rate cuts following the credit policy. Foreign exchange reserves also rose marginally to 23.58 billion dollars from 23.50 billion dollars. Special drawing rights rose to 76 million dollars from 75 million dollars.
CENTRAL BANK PROBING BOND ISSUES

The central bank (RBI) is conducting an enquiry into the bond issues of the Industrial Development Bank of India, Industrial Finance Corporation of India and Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India. The RBI seeks to find out whether the financial institutions (FIs) forwarded money to corporates on the understanding that the money would be ploughed back into the FI bond issues. RBI sources confirmed the enquiry was being conducted at a supervisory level which implies the result of the investigation may never be made public. It is probably the first time that confirmation of such an enquiry is being made.
DECLINE IN POWER GRID PERFORMANCE - WORLD BANK

Power Grid Corporation's (PGC) overall performance in project development and implementation was deteriorating due to internal problems, a World Bank evaluation report said. But it rated PGC's performance between 1991 and 1995 as satisfactory. The rating related to PGC's $1.5 billion loan agreement with the World Bank. Gains made from 1991 had eroded since late 1995 and the PGC was effectively paralysed due to leadership at the board of directors level. The Bank strongly emphasised the need for a regular chairman and managing director, a full-time finance director and reduction in the number of part-time government directors to one from the present four.
BILL TO AMEND INSURANCE LAWS IN WINTER SESSION

The government will move a bill in the forthcoming session of parliament to amend and codify insurance laws. The government is likely to incorporate amendments in the Insurance Act, Life Insurance Company Act and the General Insurance Company Act, besides vesting the Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) with statutory powers. Sources said the extent of powers given to the IRA in the proposed legislation would indicate the direction of the government's plans to liberalise the insurance sector. Even if the sector is not thrown open now, the bill is likely to enable the IRA to draw up the regulatory mechanism for a liberalised scenario.
TATA FIRMS CAN RETAIN OWN BRANDS

The Tata brand equity scheme would allow group companies to retain their individual brands if their managements decided to do so. This ended speculation over whether group companies like Indian Hotels would be able to retain their Taj brand once the brand equity scheme became operational. The scheme, broad parameters of which were finalised, envisaged the creation of a central body fund to promote a common umbrella Tata brand. It would be operational afetr formal agreements were finalised and executed among operating companies and Tata Sons, the group's parent holdng company.
The Observer
MINISTRY SEEKS POWER TO CLEAR EXPLORATION DEALS

The petroleum and natural gas ministry has sought empowerment from the government for awarding exploration contracts to private sector oil companies. The ministry's move is aimed at drastically curtailing delays in the process. At present, it is mandatory for entrepreneurs to get approvals from different government agencies including the petroleum ministry, before obtaining licence for exploration. The ministry sources said the government's efforts to woo investments in exploration through bidding during the last five years could not succeed to the desired extent mainly due to the time lag taking place in the process of awarding contracts.
